nodes.content: Infer spatial conductivity and unknown boundary flux from sparse temperature observations while preserving uncertainty under nonidentifiability.
requirements: Achieve 90% interval coverage within five percentage points for conductivity and flux across identifiability regimes.
Match known-flux conductivity reconstruction error within 20% when joint recovery is identifiable.

nodes.content: Fit a PDE-constrained hierarchical Bayesian model with Matérn conductivity and flux priors, using parallel-tempered MCMC to preserve nonidentifiable posterior ridges.
Can posterior ridge geometry distinguish conductivity–flux tradeoffs from identifiable features using only eight interior temperature sensors?
With eight sensors, posterior conductivity–flux ridge correlations exceed 0.8 in magnitude, while orthogonal uncertainty shrinks 50% versus prior.
Simulate Heat8 identifiable and confounded cases; sample tempered posteriors, then compare ridge correlations and orthogonal variance against priors.
Run four tempered chains on 200 Heat8 replicates per regime; estimate posterior ridge correlations and prior-normalized orthogonal variance.
Across 200 confounded Heat8 replicates, median ridge correlation was −0.86; orthogonal posterior variance fell 57% versus prior.
Retain joint posterior sampling rather than plug-in flux estimates, because Heat8’s −0.86 ridge correlation reveals strong confounding.
Heat8 posterior archive v1 contains four-chain conductivity–flux draws for 200 replicates per regime, plus ridge-correlation and variance diagnostics.
In identifiable Heat8 cases, median absolute conductivity–flux ridge correlation should fall below 0.4, versus 0.86 in confounded cases.
From Heat8 archive v1, compare median absolute ridge correlations across identifiable and confounded replicates using bootstrap 95% intervals.
Identifiable Heat8 replicates had median absolute ridge correlation 0.61 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.56–0.66), exceeding the predicted 0.4.
Calibrate 90% conductivity and flux intervals from joint posterior draws across Heat8 regimes; benchmark identifiable conductivity RMSE against known-flux inversion.
Score pointwise 90% interval coverage for conductivity and flux across Heat8 regimes; compare identifiable conductivity RMSE with known-flux baseline.
Heat8 benchmark v1 records regime-stratified 90% conductivity and flux coverage plus identifiable conductivity RMSE versus the known-flux baseline.
Use likelihood-informed subspace sampling to reconstruct identifiable conductivity modes while retaining prior uncertainty along conductivity–flux null modes.
Extract likelihood-informed modes; sample them by MCMC and null modes from conditional priors; test Heat8 coverage and known-flux-relative RMSE.
Using Heat8 benchmark v1, compare tempered joint MCMC and likelihood-informed sampling on regime-stratified coverage and identifiable conductivity RMSE.
Likelihood-informed sampling achieved 88–93% conductivity and flux coverage across Heat8 regimes; identifiable conductivity RMSE was 12% above known-flux baseline.
Does conditional-prior sampling of conductivity–flux null modes preserve 90% flux coverage when Heat8 sensors cluster near the flux boundary?
With six of eight sensors within 0.1 domain lengths of the flux boundary, conditional-prior null draws maintain 85–95% flux coverage.
On Heat8 benchmark v1, cluster six sensors near the flux boundary; score 90% flux coverage across 200 conditional-prior null-mode fits.
Clustered Heat8 flux coverage was 89%, supporting the null-draw hypothesis, but conductivity coverage fell to 79%, refuting p2’s uncertainty claim.
Adopt likelihood-informed sampling for standard Heat8 layouts; defer clustered layouts because conductivity coverage fell to 79%.
For deferred clustered layouts, reclassify boundary-sensitive modes, likelihood-correct remaining null draws, and reassess conductivity and flux coverage.
Recompute clustered Heat8 likelihood-informed modes, importance-reweight residual null draws, and measure 90% coverage against benchmark v1.
Heat8 clustered-layout patch v2 contains recomputed boundary-sensitive modes, likelihood-weighted null draws, and benchmark v1-compatible coverage summaries.
Use controlled interior heat pulses and time-resolved sparse thermometry to separate conductivity from unknown flux through joint posterior inference.
Optimize two Heat8 interior pulse locations by Fisher information; simulate transients and benchmark 90% coverage and known-flux-relative conductivity RMSE.
Extend Heat8 clustered-layout patch v2 with two Fisher-optimal pulses; fit 200 transients, scoring coverage and known-flux-relative conductivity RMSE.
Across 200 pulsed clustered Heat8 transients, conductivity and flux coverage reached 89% and 91%; conductivity RMSE exceeded known-flux by 14%.
Heat8-Pulse v1 contains two optimized pulse locations, 200 transient observation sets, joint posterior draws, coverage tables, and known-flux RMSE comparisons.
Fit shared conductivity and trial-specific Gaussian-process fluxes across repeated thermal trials, retaining uncertainty in unresolved conductivity–flux scaling.
Do varied unknown fluxes across repeated trials identify shared conductivity, or does a global conductivity–flux scaling ambiguity persist?
Across four distinct-flux trials, conductivity shape RMSE falls 25% versus one trial, while global-scale posterior variance barely shrinks.
Fit hierarchical posteriors to 200 four-trial Heat8 groups; compare shape RMSE and scale variance against single-trial fits.
Four-trial Heat8 reduced conductivity shape RMSE 17% versus single-trial, not 25%; global-scale posterior variance changed 3%, preserving ambiguity.
Heat8-MultiTrial v1 stores 200 four-trial groups, hierarchical posterior draws, shape RMSE comparisons, and global-scale variance diagnostics.
Add a 5%-noise total-heat calorimetry constraint to the PDE likelihood, anchoring conductivity–flux scale without prescribing flux shape.
Simulate calorimetry-augmented Heat8 regimes; fit joint posteriors and compare scale variance, 90% conductivity/flux coverage, and known-flux-relative conductivity RMSE.
Using Heat8-Pulse v1 and Heat8-MultiTrial v1, compare pulses, repeated trials, and 5%-noise calorimetry on coverage, conductivity RMSE, and scale variance.
Calorimetry cut scale variance 62% versus four trials; Heat8 conductivity/flux coverage reached 90%/92%, with identifiable RMSE 11% above known-flux.
Prioritize calorimetry for scale anchoring; use pulses when unavailable, since four trials improve shape but barely reduce scale uncertainty.
Validate the calorimetry-first workflow across sensor layouts and noise levels; retain pulsed inference as fallback and audit 90% interval coverage.
Using Heat8 clustered-layout patch v2, Heat8-Pulse v1, and Heat8-MultiTrial v1, test calorimetry-first coverage and RMSE across layouts and 2–10% noise.
Heat8 validation matrix v1 tabulates calorimetry-first and pulsed-fallback coverage, conductivity RMSE, sensor layout, and 2–10% observation noise.
